# SGDC ↔ RTL port drift census

**Snapshot: 2026-08-17.** Generated by `scripts/cdc/sgdc_port_drift.py`, which parses
the RTL directly and compares it against every `.sgdc` in the tree. No SpyGlass
licence, no tool run, no elaboration — the check is static and definitive.

```
scripts/cdc/sgdc_port_drift.py --full          # this report
scripts/cdc/sgdc_port_drift.py --markdown      # per-file markdown tables
scripts/cdc/sgdc_port_drift.py --check         # CI gate: exit 1 on any STALE
scripts/cdc/sgdc_port_drift.py --only tidelink # filter by path substring
```

> **Concurrency caveat.** `nanosoc-multicore-system/cdc/nanosoc_multicore_soc.sgdc`
> and `cdc/nanosoc_eth_chiplet.sgdc` were being actively edited by another session
> while this census ran. The numbers below are the **working tree** at 2026-08-17
> ~18:30, not `HEAD`. Where the two differ materially it is called out.

---

## Why this exists, and what the two findings mean

An `abstract_port` whose name no longer matches a real module port is dropped.
The port it was meant to constrain falls back to a default clock. That
manufactures spurious crossings at best and **masks real ones** at worst.

The governing asymmetry, which should decide every judgement call in these files:

> **A WRONG clock declaration MASKS a real crossing. A MISSING one only over-reports.**

So the two findings are not equally severe:

| Finding | Meaning | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| **STALE** | Declared in the SGDC, no such port in the RTL. The declaration is dead. If the port was *renamed* rather than deleted, the live port is now silently defaulted. | **High** |
| **UNDECLARED** | Real port, no constraint. Defaulted. | Depends on whether the default happens to be right. Over-reports; does not mask. |

The script deliberately does **not** guess the correct domain for an undeclared
port. Guessing is the failure mode it exists to catch.

not a small number, and three files below are effectively unconstrained.

## Findings that need a decision

### F1 — `ethernet_ss_ahb.sgdc` constrains a unit the SoC does not build

`nanosoc-multicore-system/ethernet-subsystem-ahb/cdc/ethernet_ss_ahb.sgdc:19`
declares `current_design ethernet_ss_ahb`. The only definition of that module
anywhere in the tree is
`ethernet-subsystem-ahb/syn/asic/gate-sim/golden/ethernet_ss_ahb.v` — a gate-sim
golden **netlist**. There is no source RTL for it.

What the SoC actually instantiates is `ethernet_ss_ahb_rmii`
(`build_soc/rtl/nanosoc_multicore_soc.sv:834`), defined in
`build_soc/rtl/ethernet_ss_ahb_rmii.sv`. A second variant,
`ethernet_ss_ahb_phc`, exists in `build_soc_phc/rtl/`.

The trap: because the stale netlist *does* still define `mtx_clk_i` / `mrx_clk_i`
and the `cpu_0_*` port family, **the SGDC's declarations validate cleanly against
it**, and the file reports 0 stale. The drift is one level up — in the
`current_design` name — where no port-level check can see it. The script now
flags this case explicitly as `[NETLIST/ARTEFACT ONLY]`.

The eth-ss CDC Makefile defaults to `MODULE ?= ethernet_ss_ahb`, so this is the
unit that flow analyses by default.

**Not fixed here** — out of scope. Needs the owner to decide whether the flow
should target `ethernet_ss_ahb_rmii`, and whether the golden netlist should be
retired.

### F2 — three subsystem SGDCs are effectively unconstrained

`phc.sgdc` (2/40 declared), `phc_ahb.sgdc` (2/42), `ethmac_ahb.sgdc` (4/40),
`ethmac_subsystem_apb.sgdc` (5/59), `tidechart.sgdc` (1/29).

These are not *wrong* — nothing is masked — but a CDC run on any of them is
mostly analysing virtual clocks. `tidechart.sgdc` is defensible: TideChart is a
genuinely single-clock design, and its header says so. The PHC and ethmac ones
are not: both straddle real clock boundaries (`rtc_time_*`, `mtx`/`mrx` pads,
PTP capture strobes) and those are exactly the ports left undeclared.

### F3 — `pad_clk_tx` has no clock object anywhere in the TideLink flow

`pad_clk_tx` and `pad_tx` are undeclared in both `tidelink_top.sgdc` and
`axi_chiplet_controller.sgdc`, and no `clock -name pad_clk_tx` exists in either.
The D2D **transmit** launch domain is therefore unmodelled, while the receive
side (`pad_clk_rx`, `link_rx_clk_o`) is fully modelled. Left undeclared
deliberately — inventing a domain here would mask, and the honest fix is to
declare the clock object first. Recorded in
`tidelink/cdc/axi_chiplet_controller.sgdc` block (a)/(d).

## Where the brief was wrong

Three claims handed to this pass did not survive checking. Recording them so they
are not re-litigated.

### W1 — `checkSGDC_05` is **not** the unmatched-`abstract_port` detector

This is asserted in `cdc/waiver.swl:84` and was the stated premise for removing
the `waive -rule checkSGDC_05` line. It is false. Per the installed rule
documentation (`$SPYGLASS_HOME/htmlhelp/spyglass/checkSGDC_05.htm`, SpyGlass
2022.06-SP2):

> *"Checks if constraints are valid for non-top environments. […] If a constraint
> is not effective in a non-top environment, that constraint is migrated to the
> top and violation is flagged."*

The real unmatched-port detectors are **`SGDC_abstract_port02`** (*"'\<port\>' not
found on/within module '\<module\>'"*) and **`SGDC_abstract_port21`**. Neither is
waived anywhere in this tree — both were live throughout. Verified by grep across
all three `waiver.swl` files.

Consequences:

* The original justification in `tidelink/cdc/waiver.swl` — *"abstract_port
  auto-migrated for stop_module'd subblocks"* — was **accurate**. That flow
  really does declare constraints under non-top `current_design` blocks for
  stop_module'd units, and checkSGDC_05 really does flag each migration.
* The `apb_ctrl_reg_rf` omission did **not** recur "because checkSGDC_05 was
  waived". No rule could have caught it: `SGDC_abstract_port02/21` fire on a
  declaration pointing at a name that no longer exists. An **omitted** port
  produces no declaration at all, so there is nothing to check — the port is
  simply defaulted. That direction is only reachable by comparing the SGDC
  against the real port list, i.e. by this script.

The waiver was still worth narrowing — it was global, silencing the rule for the
top-level SGDC too — so it is now scoped by `-file` to the two sub-block SGDCs
whose entire purpose is non-top constraint declaration. That is a tidiness fix,
not the safety fix it was billed as.

### W2 — `nanosoc_multicore_soc.sgdc` was already fixed

The brief's description matches `HEAD` exactly, but **not** the working tree.
Measured on the committed version vs the working tree, same RTL:

| | `HEAD` (99f7f7e) | working tree |
|---|--:|--:|
| ports | 114 | 114 |
| declared | 44 | **89** |
| **STALE** | **16** | **0** |

The 16 stale declarations at `HEAD` were exactly the ones described: `mtx_clk_i`
and `mrx_clk_i` (dead clocks), the six renamed `cpu_0_*`/`cpu_1_*` ports, and the
eight MII data ports hung off those dead clocks. All are fixed in the working
tree — `mtx_clk_i`/`mrx_clk_i` are now the hierarchical
`u_network_core/mtx_clk_w` / `mrx_clk_w`, and the CPU ports are
`network_core_*`/`chip_core_*`.

The `phc_pps_out` / `phc_pps_irq` / `phc_alarm_irq` wrong-clock claim is likewise
already fixed: they were on `rtc_clk` at `HEAD` and are on `sys_fclk` in the
working tree, with an in-file comment describing precisely the masking the brief
attributed to them. **One residual worth an owner's eye:** the launching flop is
`u_phc_0`, instantiated with `.HCLK(u_network_core_sys_hclk)`
(`build_soc/rtl/nanosoc_multicore_soc.sv:1037`) — the *network core's* `sys_hclk`,
not `sys_fclk`. Whether `sys_hclk` is in the `sys_fclk` domain (buffered) or a
derived clock decides whether `sys_fclk` is exactly right or merely close. Not
investigated here; that file is owned by another session.

### W3 — the TideLink waiver hole was wider than three regexps

The brief named `-du Wlink*`, `-du Wav*`, `-du wlink_*`. Also unsound, and also
now removed: the exact-name waivers `-du "ShortPacketToWlink"`,
`-du "TideLinkToWlink"`, `-du "i2c_master"` and `-du "axi_chiplet_controller"` —
all four name modules with locally-modified copies in
`tidelink/src/rtl/local_overrides/`. See `docs/` note in
`tidelink/cdc/waiver.swl` and `scripts/cdc/gen_tidelink_waivers.py --check`.

## Method, and what this check cannot do

* **Port extraction** parses the module header directly (ANSI and non-ANSI
  styles). Preprocessor conditionals are kept in **both** arms, so the port set
  is a superset. That is the safe direction: an extra port shows up as
  UNDECLARED (over-report); a dropped one would hide real drift.
* **Multiple definitions.** `tidelink_top`, `axi_chiplet_controller` and
  `nanosoc_multicore_soc` each have several copies — packaged-IP snapshots under
  `tidelink/imp/fpga/*/src/` and gate experiments under `tidelink/imp/hw_gate/`.
  The script picks by path precedence (`src/rtl/local_overrides/` > `src/rtl/` >
  `rtl/` > `logical/` > `deps/`, build artefacts last) and flags a port-set
  disagreement. Verify the `RTL resolved to` column matches the flist your flow
  actually reads.
* **Hierarchical names** (`u_network_core/mtx_clk_w`,
  `u_apb_qspi_regs/reg13[*]`) are reported but not checked — they are not ports
  of the current design by construction. Four exist tree-wide.
* **This check cannot detect a wrong clock domain.** It verifies that a name
  exists, not that the domain assigned to it is true. Wrong-domain findings
  require reading the RTL, and the two in this document (F3, W2) were found that
  way. That gap is why the asymmetry rule matters: the automatable half of the
  problem is the half that only over-reports.
* **Build-conditional ports** are a genuine limitation of the SGDC format, which
  has no preprocessor. An `abstract_port` for a port behind an `` `ifdef `` is
  **fatal** in a build where the define is absent (`SGDC_abstract_port02`, exit
  code 7, a run that reports "0 clocks / 0 crossings" and reads like a tool
  fault). `axi_chiplet_controller` has three such ports; the chiplet SGDC
  declares them (its default flist defines `TIDELINK_PHY_V2`), the TideLink SGDC
  deliberately does not (its default flist does not). Both are correct for their
  own default build. A drift report cannot tell these apart from real omissions —
  read the `NOT DECLARED` blocks in each file before acting on a count.

---

## Making this a CI gate

`--check` exits 1 on any stale declaration. It is safe to turn on **today**:
the tree is at 0.

```yaml
- name: SGDC port drift
  run: scripts/cdc/sgdc_port_drift.py --check
```

Companion gate for the waiver hole, likewise green today:

```yaml
- name: TideLink CDC waiver soundness
  run: scripts/cdc/gen_tidelink_waivers.py --check
```

Neither needs a licence, a tool install, or elaboration. A full pass takes a few
minutes, dominated by reading ~11k RTL files.

Note that `--check` gates only the STALE direction. The UNDECLARED count (428)
is a backlog, not a regression signal; ratcheting it would need a per-file
baseline, which is deliberately not done here — several of those omissions are
correct, and a baseline would freeze the wrong ones in place.
